title: Invert Binary Tree
description: At {{companyName}}, the {{department}} traffic routing service stores its primary and replica zone hierarchy as a binary tree with root node root. To switch to the mirrored failover layout across {{location}}, as a {{roleTitle}} in {{domain}}, invert the tree by swapping the left and right child of every node, and return its root.
ioNote: Trees are given in level-order as an array where null marks a missing child (the same format used by LeetCode). An empty array means an empty tree. A returned tree is serialized the same way (trailing nulls removed).

title: Same Tree
description: At {{companyName}}, the {{department}} configuration management service compares two deployment dependency trees p and q before approving a rollout. As a {{roleTitle}} in {{domain}}, determine whether the two binary trees are identical, meaning they have the same structure and the same node values.
constraints: 0 <= number of nodes in each tree <= 100
ioNote: Trees are given in level-order as an array where null marks a missing child (the same format used by LeetCode). An empty array means an empty tree.

title: Binary Tree Inorder Traversal
description: At {{companyName}}, the {{department}} indexing engine stores catalog keys in a binary search tree with root node root. As a {{roleTitle}} in {{domain}}, return the inorder traversal (left, node, right) of its node values so keys can be emitted for a batch export.
ioNote: Trees are given in level-order as an array where null marks a missing child (the same format used by LeetCode). An empty array means an empty tree.

title: Binary Tree Level Order Traversal
description: At {{companyName}}, the {{department}} organizational chart service models reporting lines as a binary tree rooted at root. To produce a tier-by-tier escalation report for {{location}}, as a {{roleTitle}} in {{domain}}, return the level order traversal of the node values, from left to right, level by level.
ioNote: Trees are given in level-order as an array where null marks a missing child (the same format used by LeetCode). An empty array means an empty tree.

title: Path Sum
description: At {{companyName}}, the {{department}} rules engine evaluates a decision tree with root node root, where each node carries a weighted score. As a {{roleTitle}} in {{domain}}, determine whether the tree has a root-to-leaf path whose node values add up to targetSum. A leaf is a node with no children.
ioNote: Trees are given in level-order as an array where null marks a missing child (the same format used by LeetCode). An empty array means an empty tree.

title: Diameter of Binary Tree
description: At {{companyName}}, the {{department}} network backbone is modeled as a binary tree with root node root. As a {{roleTitle}} in {{domain}}, compute the diameter of the tree: the length of the longest path between any two nodes, which may or may not pass through the root. The length of a path is the number of edges on it.
ioNote: Trees are given in level-order as an array where null marks a missing child (the same format used by LeetCode). An empty array means an empty tree.

title: Balanced Binary Tree
description: At {{companyName}}, the {{department}} load-balancing layer arranges its worker pools as a binary tree with root node root. To keep lookups fast across {{location}}, as a {{roleTitle}} in {{domain}}, determine whether the tree is height-balanced, meaning the depths of the two subtrees of every node never differ by more than one.
ioNote: Trees are given in level-order as an array where null marks a missing child (the same format used by LeetCode). An empty array means an empty tree.

title: Validate Binary Search Tree
description: At {{companyName}}, the {{department}} ordered key index is persisted as a binary tree with root node root. Before serving queries in {{location}}, as a {{roleTitle}} in {{domain}}, verify that the tree is a valid binary search tree: every left subtree holds strictly smaller keys, every right subtree holds strictly larger keys, and both subtrees are themselves valid.
ioNote: Trees are given in level-order as an array where null marks a missing child (the same format used by LeetCode). An empty array means an empty tree.

title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a BST
description: At {{companyName}}, the {{department}} access-control service stores its permission hierarchy as a binary search tree with root node root. As a {{roleTitle}} in {{domain}}, find the lowest common ancestor of the nodes holding values p and q. The lowest common ancestor is the deepest node that has both nodes as descendants, where a node may be a descendant of itself.
constraints: p != q and both p and q exist in the tree
ioNote: Trees are given in level-order as an array where null marks a missing child (the same format used by LeetCode). An empty array means an empty tree. p and q are node values; return the value of their lowest common ancestor.

title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Tree
description: At {{companyName}}, the {{department}} dependency graph for microservices in {{location}} is represented as a binary tree with root node root. As a {{roleTitle}} in {{domain}}, find the lowest common ancestor of the nodes holding values p and q, i.e. the deepest node that has both as descendants (a node may be a descendant of itself).
constraints: p != q and both p and q exist in the tree
ioNote: Trees are given in level-order as an array where null marks a missing child (the same format used by LeetCode). An empty array means an empty tree. p and q are node values; return the value of their lowest common ancestor.

title: Binary Tree Right Side View
description: At {{companyName}}, the {{department}} monitoring dashboard renders a service hierarchy, a binary tree with root node root, as seen from the right side. As a {{roleTitle}} in {{domain}}, return the values of the nodes you can see ordered from top to bottom.
ioNote: Trees are given in level-order as an array where null marks a missing child (the same format used by LeetCode). An empty array means an empty tree.

title: Kth Smallest Element in a BST
description: At {{companyName}}, the {{department}} leaderboard service keeps latency scores in a binary search tree with root node root. As a {{roleTitle}} in {{domain}}, return the k-th smallest score (1-indexed) among all values in the tree.
constraints: The tree is a valid binary search tree
ioNote: Trees are given in level-order as an array where null marks a missing child (the same format used by LeetCode). An empty array means an empty tree.

title: Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum
description: At {{companyName}}, the {{department}} profit-and-loss rollup models regional net results as a binary tree with root node root. As a {{roleTitle}} in {{domain}}, find the maximum path sum. A path is a sequence of nodes in which each adjacent pair is connected by an edge, each node appears at most once, and the path need not pass through the root.
ioNote: Trees are given in level-order as an array where null marks a missing child (the same format used by LeetCode). An empty array means an empty tree.

title: Construct Binary Tree from Preorder and Inorder Traversal
description: At {{companyName}}, the {{department}} disaster-recovery job in {{location}} must rebuild a lost hierarchy from two logged traversals, preorder and inorder, of the same binary tree. As a {{roleTitle}} in {{domain}}, construct and return the binary tree.
constraints: All values are unique and both arrays describe the same tree
ioNote: The returned tree is serialized in level-order as an array where null marks a missing child (trailing nulls removed).

title: Binary Tree Zigzag Level Order Traversal
description: At {{companyName}}, the {{department}} audit service walks a binary tree with root node root in an alternating pattern to balance read pressure across {{location}}. As a {{roleTitle}} in {{domain}}, return the zigzag level order traversal: left to right on the first level, right to left on the next, and so on.
ioNote: Trees are given in level-order as an array where null marks a missing child (the same format used by LeetCode). An empty array means an empty tree.

title: Count Good Nodes in Binary Tree
description: At {{companyName}}, the {{department}} capacity planner stores node capacities in a binary tree with root node root. A node X is considered good if no node on the path from the root to X has a value greater than X. As a {{roleTitle}} in {{domain}}, return the number of good nodes in the tree.
ioNote: Trees are given in level-order as an array where null marks a missing child (the same format used by LeetCode). An empty array means an empty tree.

title: Sum Root to Leaf Numbers
description: At {{companyName}}, the {{department}} routing-code generator stores digit nodes (0-9) in a binary tree with root node root. Each root-to-leaf path spells out a numeric routing code. As a {{roleTitle}} in {{domain}}, return the total sum of all root-to-leaf numbers.
constraints: Tree depth is at most 10 (the answer fits in 32 bits)
ioNote: Trees are given in level-order as an array where null marks a missing child (the same format used by LeetCode). An empty array means an empty tree.

title: Course Schedule
description: At {{companyName}}, the {{department}} learning platform assigns {{roleTitle}} onboarding modules numbered 0 to numCourses - 1 across {{location}}. Prerequisites are given as pairs [a, b] meaning module b must be completed before module a. As a {{roleTitle}} in {{domain}}, determine whether it is possible to finish all modules.
constraints: prerequisites[i] = [a, b] means course b must be taken before course a

title: Course Schedule II
description: At {{companyName}}, the {{department}} learning platform must schedule modules numbered 0 to numCourses - 1 given prerequisites as pairs [a, b], meaning module b must be completed before module a. As a {{roleTitle}} in {{domain}}, return an ordering of modules that satisfies every prerequisite. If several orderings exist, return any of them. If it is impossible, return an empty array.
constraints: prerequisites[i] = [a, b] means course b must be taken before course a
ioNote: Multiple valid answers exist. Grade with a checker that verifies the result is a permutation of 0..numCourses-1 satisfying every prerequisite, or is empty when no valid order exists. expectedOutput is one valid answer (Kahn's BFS order).

title: Rotting Oranges
description: At {{companyName}}'s {{location}} cold-storage facility, the {{department}} monitoring system tracks an m x n grid where 0 is an empty shelf, 1 is a fresh crate and 2 is a spoiled crate. Every minute, each fresh crate that is 4-directionally adjacent to a spoiled crate becomes spoiled. As a {{roleTitle}} in {{domain}}, return the minimum number of minutes until no fresh crate remains, or -1 if that is impossible.

title: Pacific Atlantic Water Flow
description: At {{companyName}}'s {{location}} campus, the {{department}} drainage model uses an m x n matrix heights where heights[r][c] is the elevation of cell (r, c). The Pacific drains from the top and left edges and the Atlantic from the bottom and right edges. Water flows 4-directionally to cells of equal or lower height. As a {{roleTitle}} in {{domain}}, return all cells from which water can reach both oceans.
ioNote: Return cells as [row, col] pairs. Compare as unordered sets. expectedOutput is sorted for convenience.

title: Surrounded Regions
description: At {{companyName}}'s {{location}} facility, the {{department}} zoning engine represents floor plots as an m x n board of 'X' (blocked) and 'O' (open) cells. As a {{roleTitle}} in {{domain}}, capture every region of 'O' cells that is fully surrounded by 'X' in all four directions by flipping those 'O' cells to 'X'. Regions touching the border are never captured.
ioNote: board is an array of rows of single-character strings. Return the resulting board (it may be modified in place and returned).

title: Number of Provinces
description: At {{companyName}}, the {{department}} partner network is described by an n x n matrix isConnected where isConnected[i][j] = 1 means partners i and j are directly linked, and connectivity is transitive. As a {{roleTitle}} in {{domain}}, return the total number of provinces, where a province is a maximal group of directly or indirectly connected partners.
constraints: isConnected[i][i] == 1 and the matrix is symmetric

title: Is Graph Bipartite?
description: At {{companyName}}, the {{department}} scheduling service must split conflicting jobs across two worker pools in {{location}}. The conflicts form an undirected graph given as an adjacency list graph, where graph[u] lists the nodes adjacent to u. As a {{roleTitle}} in {{domain}}, determine whether the nodes can be partitioned into two sets such that every edge connects a node from one set to a node from the other (the graph may be disconnected).
constraints: No self-loops or parallel edges; if v is in graph[u] then u is in graph[v]

title: Find if Path Exists in Graph
description: At {{companyName}}, the {{department}} connectivity checker verifies reachability between n data centers numbered 0 to n - 1, linked by bidirectional cables given in the array edges. As a {{roleTitle}} in {{domain}}, determine whether a valid path exists from the data center source to the data center destination.
constraints: No self-loops and no duplicate edges

title: Network Delay Time
description: At {{companyName}}, the {{department}} messaging backbone connects n nodes labeled 1 to n. The array times holds directed links [u, v, w], meaning a signal travels from u to v in w time units. As a {{roleTitle}} in {{domain}}, a signal is sent from node k. Return the minimum time for all n nodes to receive it, or -1 if some node can never receive it.

title: Min Cost to Connect All Points
description: At {{companyName}}, the {{department}} infrastructure team is laying fiber between sensor sites in {{location}}, given as 2D coordinates in the array points. The cost of connecting two sites is their Manhattan distance |xi - xj| + |yi - yj|. As a {{roleTitle}} in {{domain}}, return the minimum total cost to connect all sites so that exactly one simple path exists between any two of them.

title: Redundant Connection
description: At {{companyName}}, the {{department}} network topology was a tree of n nodes labeled 1 to n until one extra cable was added, creating a cycle. The links are given in the array edges. As a {{roleTitle}} in {{domain}}, return an edge that can be removed so the graph is a tree again. If several answers exist, return the one that occurs last in the input.
constraints: edges[i] = [a, b] with 1 <= a < b <= n
No repeated edges; the graph is connected

title: Number of Connected Components in an Undirected Graph
description: At {{companyName}}, the {{department}} cluster manager tracks n servers labeled 0 to n - 1 joined by undirected links listed in edges. As a {{roleTitle}} in {{domain}}, return the number of connected components, meaning groups of servers that can reach each other either directly or indirectly.

title: Shortest Path in Binary Matrix
description: At {{companyName}}'s {{location}} fulfillment center, the {{department}} robot navigator moves across an n x n grid where 0 is a clear cell and 1 is an obstacle. Robots may move to any of the 8 neighboring cells. As a {{roleTitle}} in {{domain}}, return the length (number of cells) of the shortest clear path from the top-left cell to the bottom-right cell, or -1 if none exists.

title: Walls and Gates
description: At {{companyName}}'s {{location}} warehouse, the {{department}} layout planner models the floor as an m x n grid where -1 is a wall, 0 is an exit gate and 2147483647 (INF) is an empty room. As a {{roleTitle}} in {{domain}}, fill each empty room with the distance (in 4-directional steps) to its nearest gate. If a gate cannot be reached, leave the room as INF.
ioNote: INF = 2147483647. Return the resulting grid (it may be modified in place and returned).

title: Path With Minimum Effort
description: At {{companyName}}, the {{department}} drone-delivery planner uses a rows x columns grid heights of terrain elevations for {{location}}. A drone starts at the top-left cell and must reach the bottom-right cell, moving 4-directionally. As a {{roleTitle}} in {{domain}}, find a route that minimizes the maximum absolute elevation difference between consecutive cells along the route, and return that value.

title: Critical Connections in a Network
description: At {{companyName}}, the {{department}} reliability team maintains n servers numbered 0 to n - 1 connected by undirected links in the array connections across {{location}}. A link is critical if removing it disconnects some servers from others. As a {{roleTitle}} in {{domain}}, return all critical connections in the network, in any order.
constraints: No repeated connections; the network is connected
ioNote: Compare as an unordered set of unordered pairs (each pair may be returned as [a, b] or [b, a]). expectedOutput lists each pair with a < b, sorted.

title: Find the City With the Smallest Number of Neighbors at a Threshold Distance
description: At {{companyName}}, the {{department}} logistics team has n hubs numbered 0 to n - 1 joined by weighted bidirectional lanes edges[i] = [from, to, weight] across {{location}}. As a {{roleTitle}} in {{domain}}, return the hub with the fewest other hubs reachable within a shortest-path distance of at most distanceThreshold. If several hubs tie, return the one with the greatest number.

title: House Robber
description: At {{companyName}}, the {{department}} batch scheduler in {{location}} can claim compute credits from a row of nodes, where nums[i] is the credit on node i. Claiming two adjacent nodes triggers an anti-abuse lock. As a {{roleTitle}} in {{domain}}, return the maximum total credit that can be claimed without choosing two adjacent nodes.

title: House Robber II
description: At {{companyName}}, the {{department}} credit allocator now manages nodes arranged in a ring, so the first and last nodes are adjacent. nums[i] is the credit on node i, and claiming two adjacent nodes triggers a lock. As a {{roleTitle}} in {{domain}}, return the maximum total credit that can be claimed without choosing two adjacent nodes.

title: Unique Paths
description: At {{companyName}}'s {{location}} data hall, a maintenance robot starts at the top-left of an m x n rack grid and must reach the bottom-right, moving only right or down. As a {{roleTitle}} in {{domain}}, return the number of distinct paths the robot can take.
constraints: The answer fits in a 32-bit signed integer

title: Minimum Path Sum
description: At {{companyName}}, the {{department}} cost-routing service models transit fees as an m x n grid of non-negative costs. As a {{roleTitle}} in {{domain}}, find the path from the top-left to the bottom-right cell, moving only right or down, that minimizes the sum of the costs along it, and return that sum.

title: Partition Equal Subset Sum
description: At {{companyName}}, the {{department}} billing reconciler in {{location}} receives a list of invoice amounts nums. As a {{roleTitle}} in {{domain}}, determine whether the amounts can be split into two groups whose totals are exactly equal.

title: 0/1 Knapsack
description: At {{companyName}}'s {{location}} depot, a freight carrier has a weight capacity W. Cargo item i has weight wt[i] and market value val[i], and each item can be loaded whole or not at all. As a {{roleTitle}} in {{domain}}, return the maximum total value that fits in the carrier.

title: Longest Palindromic Subsequence
description: At {{companyName}}, the {{department}} data-integrity team scans event logs, represented as a string s, for symmetric patterns. As a {{roleTitle}} in {{domain}}, return the length of the longest palindromic subsequence of s. A subsequence keeps the relative order of the remaining characters after deleting zero or more characters.
constraints: s consists only of lowercase English letters

title: Decode Ways
description: At {{companyName}}, the {{department}} legacy gateway encodes messages by mapping A to 1, B to 2, ..., Z to 26, and sends the digits as a string s. As a {{roleTitle}} in {{domain}}, return the number of distinct ways the digit string can be decoded back into letters. Return 0 if it cannot be decoded.
constraints: s contains only digits and may contain leading zeros
The answer fits in a 32-bit integer

title: Maximal Square
description: At {{companyName}}'s {{location}} data center, the {{department}} capacity map is an m x n matrix of '0' and '1' cells, where '1' marks a usable rack slot. As a {{roleTitle}} in {{domain}}, find the largest square made up only of '1' cells and return its area.
ioNote: matrix is an array of rows of single-character strings '0' or '1'. Return the area (side * side).

title: Target Sum
description: At {{companyName}}, the {{department}} forecasting job receives an array nums of daily adjustments. For each value it must pick a '+' or '-' sign. As a {{roleTitle}} in {{domain}}, return the number of sign assignments whose resulting expression evaluates to target.

title: Coin Change II
description: At {{companyName}}'s {{location}} payments hub, the {{department}} gateway must settle a payout amount using the denominations in coins, with an unlimited supply of each. As a {{roleTitle}} in {{domain}}, return the number of distinct combinations of coins that sum to amount, or 0 if none do.
constraints: The answer fits in a 32-bit integer

title: Regular Expression Matching
description: At {{companyName}}, the {{department}} log-filtering engine supports patterns with '.' (matches any single character) and '*' (matches zero or more of the preceding element). As a {{roleTitle}} in {{domain}}, implement matching between an input string s and a pattern p, and return whether the pattern matches the entire string.
constraints: s contains only lowercase English letters
p contains only lowercase letters, '.' and '*'
Every '*' is preceded by a valid character

title: Burst Balloons
description: At {{companyName}}, the {{department}} ad-inventory optimizer in {{location}} holds n slots, each with a value nums[i]. Releasing slot i earns nums[i - 1] * nums[i] * nums[i + 1] points, where a neighbor outside the array counts as 1. As a {{roleTitle}} in {{domain}}, return the maximum points achievable by releasing all slots in the best possible order.

title: Interleaving String
description: At {{companyName}}, the {{department}} stream merger weaves two ordered event feeds s1 and s2 into a single feed s3. As a {{roleTitle}} in {{domain}}, determine whether s3 can be formed by interleaving s1 and s2, meaning both are split into substrings that alternate while the order of characters within each feed is preserved.
constraints: All strings consist of lowercase English letters

title: Distinct Subsequences
description: At {{companyName}}, the {{department}} pattern-matching service in {{location}} counts how often a signature string t occurs inside a raw telemetry string s. As a {{roleTitle}} in {{domain}}, return the number of distinct subsequences of s that equal t.
constraints: s and t consist of English letters
The answer fits in a 32-bit signed integer

title: Palindrome Partitioning II
description: At {{companyName}}, the {{department}} archival service splits a log string s into segments so that every segment is a palindrome, enabling symmetric compression across {{location}}. As a {{roleTitle}} in {{domain}}, return the minimum number of cuts needed to partition s so that every substring is a palindrome.
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters only
